title: I am (Mark 14:53–65)
hookLine: before the high priest, silent until asked: are you the Christ? I am

lines: THE HIGH PRIEST'S HOUSE, AT NIGHT.
cards: The same night. They lead Jesus from the garden to the high priest, and the chief priests, elders and scribes gather there. Outside in the courtyard, Peter has followed at a distance and is warming his hands at a fire.
Hold on to him; he's tomorrow. Inside, the council is looking for testimony that will stick. Witness after witness stands up, and their stories don't match.
Some say they heard Jesus threaten to destroy the temple and build another in three days. Even on that, Mark says, they don't agree. Through all of it, the man on trial says nothing.

teach.b: Finally the high priest stands up in the middle of the room. Aren't you going to answer? What is it these men testify against you?
Silence. In the King James Bible: "But he held his peace, and answered nothing." Accused, it's easy to start talking fast: explaining, correcting, defending.
He doesn't. The false stories fall apart on their own.

Then the high priest asks the one question that matters: "Art thou the Christ, the Son of the Blessed? And Jesus said, I am." The Son of the Blessed is a respectful way of saying God without saying the name.
And notice the change. Again and again in Mark, Jesus has told people to keep quiet about who he is. Now, on trial, with everything to lose, he answers plainly.
The silence and the answer come from the same place: he isn't reacting to pressure; he knows what is worth saying.
In Greek, I am is two words, ego eimi: ordinary Greek, the way anyone would say it's me. Some readers also hear an echo of the burning bush, where God tells Moses his name is I am that I am.
Readers differ on how much Mark means that here.

teach.h: THE SON OF MAN, WITH THE CLOUDS.
teach.b: Then Jesus adds a line from Daniel and the Psalms: they will see the Son of man sitting at the right hand of power, coming with the clouds of heaven.
The high priest tears his clothes, the council calls it blasphemy and condemns him, and some begin to spit and strike him, and mock him: prophesy!

how: Christians read Jesus's trial before the council in Holy Week, and many churches read the whole passion story aloud on Palm Sunday or Good Friday, often with different readers taking the parts.

Mark says their testimony didn't agree, even about the temple.

"I am." after a whole gospel of telling people to keep quiet.

games.q: you're on trial at night. false witnesses contradict each other. then the high priest asks: are you the Christ? what does Jesus do?
o: point out that the witnesses disagree.
games.why: silent through the false testimony, he answers the one real question: "I am." and adds that they will see the Son of man coming with the clouds.

practice: Picture a moment where you might feel accused, rushed or judged, a meeting, a text thread, a family dinner, and picture not rushing to defend yourself: just a breath, then another, noticing the urge to explain in your chest and jaw without obeying it.
Then ask: if I speak, what is the one true thing worth saying? If you pray, hold that moment before God in the quiet.

wordCard.voice: I am. Two plain words, ego eimi in Greek, spoken after a long silence, when the high priest asks if he is the Christ.

orig.note: Greek: I am. ordinary words, and to some readers an echo of God's name at the burning bush.

carryVoice: Your line: silence can be strong. And two plain words can be enough. Day two hundred twenty-three.
